name: Fondation Zinsou
funding: Private, with no Beninese public aid. Its undated patrons page lists BNP Paribas, Masathis, Institut Français de Paris, Agence Française de Développement and Open Society Foundations.

name: Proyecto mARTadero
funding: Its supporters page, dated 2019, names Misereor and Oxfam Internacional as current supporters, and Hivos, Conexión, Solidar Suiza, Cooperación Italiana and CAF as former ones.

name: Kiosko Galería
funding: Kiosko is a project of Fundación RSV.

name: Thapong Visual Arts Centre
funding: Board-run centre funded by the Ministry of Youth, Sport and Culture (P2.2M for the 2014 refit). Partners: HB Botswana (2024), BTC Foundation (2018), DTC Botswana and FNB Foundation (2014).

name: Casa França-Brasil
funding: Rio de Janeiro state cultural centre; restoration backed by Fundação Roberto Marinho (media).

name: Instituto Tunga
funding: Artist's estate institute. The Tunga catalogue raisonné it leads is sponsored by Itaú and Sabesp under the Rouanet Law.

name: Museu do Amanhã
funding: Run by IDG with the City of Rio and Fundação Roberto Marinho. Itaú is strategic sponsor. Shell, Instituto Cultural Vale and Motiva are maintainers. IBM, TAG and Bloomberg also give.

name: Museu de Arte Moderna da Bahia
Instituto Tomie Ohtake
funding: Nubank (R$10M a year to 2027, about 40% of budget), Bradesco, Motiva, Instituto Votorantim, Bloomberg, Usiminas and others. 98% of funds come through the Rouanet tax law; free entry.

name: Sofia City Art Gallery
funding: Sofia Municipality funds yearly acquisitions, resumed in 2007. Partners listed: Ministry of Culture, America for Bulgaria Foundation, Aurubis Bulgaria, Institut français and Goethe-Institut. No budget is published.

name: Laongo Granite Sculpture Symposium
funding: Burkina Faso's culture ministry organises it and pays professional artists' fees, flights and stay, per its 2024 call for applications. No other funder is named.
